clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old man presented with left-sided flank pain, nausea, and vomiting after a twisting injury. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT angiography revealed left renal non-enhancement secondary to suspected acute traumatic left renal artery dissection. After multidisciplinary discussion, heparin anticoagulation was initiated to attempt renal salvage. Despite treatment, the patient developed renal necrosis and ultimately required nephrectomy. Physical exam and renal function laboratory data were not documented in the available evidence.
